scope: Prostate carcinoma, WHO Classification of Urinary and Male Genital Tumours 5th ed. (2022). Grading (Gleason/ISUP Grade Groups) is the classification spine. Internal substrate only.

classification_records.morphology: Infiltrative small glands lacking basal cells; diagnosis integrates architecture, nucleomegaly/nucleoli, and basal-cell absence.
classification_records.grading_system: Gleason score -> ISUP Grade Group 1-5 (the central classification axis)
classification_records.clinical_note: The dominant prostate cancer. Grading drives risk stratification more than subtype; the basal-cell/AMACR/NKX3.1 IHC triad confirms malignancy on small foci.

classification_records.grading_system: 5-tier Grade Group system; cribriform pattern 4 and intraductal carcinoma are adverse features reported separately
classification_records.clinical_note: Grade Group is the single most important pathology output for prostate risk. Cribriform and intraductal carcinoma are independently adverse and must be flagged.

classification_records.morphology: Malignant epithelial proliferation filling/expanding ducts and acini WITH basal cells retained; dense cribriform/solid or marked nuclear atypia.
molecular_signature: associated with high-grade invasive cancer and adverse genomics (PTEN loss, BRCA2)
classification_records.grading_system: Reported as an adverse feature; not assigned a Gleason grade itself by convention
classification_records.clinical_note: Near-always associated with aggressive invasive cancer; its presence on biopsy changes management. A high-value distinct article.

classification_records.entity: Neuroendocrine / small cell carcinoma of prostate (incl. treatment-emergent)
classification_records.morphology: High-grade small/large-cell neuroendocrine morphology; may emerge after androgen-deprivation therapy.
ihc_signature: NKX3.1 often retained as lineage marker
molecular_signature: RB1 and TP53 loss; lineage plasticity from adenocarcinoma
classification_records.clinical_note: Aggressive; the treatment-emergent NE phenotype (post-ADT lineage switch) is a distinct, clinically important entity.

notes: Prostate differs from the others: GRADING (ISUP Grade Group) is the classification spine, not subtype. The basal-cell/AMACR/NKX3.1 IHC triad is the diagnostic workhorse. Cribriform pattern 4 and IDC-P are the adverse-feature articles. Verify grading conventions at write time.
